title: Choose the visual world for SepsisSentinel
question: The roll assigned the Gallery Label world: each bed shown as a numbered exhibit with an object label. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Gallery Label
options.lineage: science-museum medicine galleries: painted walls, mounted object labels, numbered exhibits
options.thesis: Every bed is a numbered exhibit with an object label; ground truth is revealed as the label's last line.
options.viewport: Wall-green top band holding the replay clock; a ranked gallery of 24 numbered beds on the left; the open exhibit's risk trajectory beside its object label (who, when, what the model saw); a numbered tour rail of six stops for the presenter.
options.risk: Can drift into a museum website instead of a working tool if the labels grow into posters.

raised.raise: One type family at a strict five-step size scale; no ad-hoc sizes anywhere (specimen discipline).
Catalogue discipline: every bed and every result keeps one number used identically on every screen.
Focus dims the wall: opening an exhibit quiets everything else on screen.
One elevation rule: only the exhibit in focus sits on a label board; everything else is wall.

options.label: Observation Chart
options.lineage: hospital track-and-trigger observation charts (NEWS2-style A3 paper charts)
options.thesis: The ward drawn as one early-warning obs chart: hourly columns, banded escalation zones, plotted risk.
options.viewport: Every bed is one row on a shared hour axis with OK / Watch / Alert bands; the current hour column is lit; selecting a row opens its full chart and reasons below.
options.risk: The most familiar direction: closest to existing clinical dashboards, and it can slide into grey hospital-legacy software.

options.label: Departure Board
options.thesis: The ward as a departures board: beds ranked by risk, status flaps cascading when an alert changes.
options.viewport: A black board of fixed columns (bed, age/sex, risk, last 12 h, status, in alert); rows re-rank with a character cascade each replay hour; the open bed slides out as a detail panel.
options.case: Fuses cleanly for the ward (ranked live rows with status flips); loses on the patient story and the evidence pages.
options.risk: A black board in a bright exhibition hall, and the cascade can tip into gimmick.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: The demo as a signed route: yellow bands name where you are in the story and what comes next.
options.viewport: A yellow band across the top names the current stop (Bed 03 · caught 6 h early) and the next; monumental bed numbers; the ward and chart below in black and white.
options.case: Wins audience recognition (everyone reads airport signs in seconds); loses on clarity because its yellow collides with the amber Watch state.
options.risk: Yellow everywhere fights the state colours and can feel like a lobby screen.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: Pixel display type at poster scale over fine text.
options.viewport: A pixel headline over dense columns.
options.case: Fuses poorly: pixel type costs legibility for a clinical subject and says nothing about sepsis.
options.kept: One family at a strict size scale, no ad-hoc sizes.

options.label: Acetate Manual
options.thesis: Sections as coloured divider boards under acetate leaves.
options.viewport: A tab rail down the edge, acetate leaves over a section hue.
options.case: Fuses poorly: visitors don't know the artifact, and seven section hues fight the state colours.
options.kept: A single elevation rule: only the item in focus is lifted.

options.label: Streaming Wall
options.thesis: Beds as poster tiles in horizontal rows.
options.viewport: Rows of bed tiles, the focused one expanding.
options.case: Fuses poorly: patients as entertainment tiles is the wrong register, and it reads as consumer product.
options.kept: Focus dims everything else on screen.

options.label: Catalogue Sleeve
options.thesis: Everything gets a catalogue number; colour codes replace words.
options.viewport: A pulse plot on black with a FAC number.
options.case: Fuses poorly: coded colour strips hide meaning, the opposite of status-by-word.
options.kept: Every item keeps one catalogue number everywhere.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean clinical analytics dashboard, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar navigation, a KPI strip, the ranked bed table and a selected-patient chart.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any analytics product by design, close to the startup-SaaS look you ruled out.
